scenes.narration_segment: Across this entire bridge — four hundred and fifty-six metres, end to end — the water falls two and a half centimetres. A drop that small is invisible; you'd swear it was level. Holding it across fifty kilometres of hills may be the most precise thing the Romans ever built — and it starts with a man whose job was counting water.
